_doc: Hand-kept facts and assumptions. Every number used in the report traces to an entry here or to live data. Addresses are Ethereum mainnet, lowercase.

ethereum.label: Ethereum mainnet (settlement)
ethereum.basis: No fund-losing consensus failure since the Merge; finality was lost twice for ~1h on 2023-05-11/12. Modelled as a 1%/yr liveness event costing ~0.5% (stuck exit, gas spike).

dependencies: Delta-hedged perp shorts on CEXs (funding-rate risk)

depeg.basis: USDe printed ~0.65 on a single CEX order book during the 2025-10-10 liquidation cascade while on-chain pools stayed near peg, and dipped ~0.3% in Apr-2024 on negative funding. Modelled: 12%/yr chance of a depeg averaging ~8%, 75% of it recovered by the horizon.

hack.basis: Loss of a custodian or CEX holding hedges; Ethena's reserve fund covers the first slice. Mean ~29% of backing.

dependencies: Ethereum validator set run by Lido node operators

depeg.basis: stETH/ETH traded ~0.94 in Jun-2022 (3AC/Celsius forced selling); withdrawals since Shapella cap the gap.

hack.basis: Mass slashing or key compromise; mean ~11%.

dependencies: Sky vaults (ETH, RWA, USDC via PSM)

depeg.basis: DAI briefly ~0.90 during the Mar-2023 USDC depeg (PSM exposure).

hack.basis: Governance or oracle attack on the CDP system.

0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb.basis: Fiat-backed; depegged to ~0.88 on 2023-03-11 (SVB). For a borrower, a loan-asset depeg lowers the debt: no loss channel.

0xdac17f958d2ee523a2206206994597c13d831e.basis: Fiat/treasury-backed. For a borrower, a loan-asset depeg lowers the debt: no loss channel.

pendle.label: Pendle V2 (AMM, SY/PT/YT contracts)
pendle.basis: A core-contract or SY-adapter exploit reaches PT holders directly. Mean ~14%: Pendle paused and protected ~$105M during the 2024-09 Penpie exploit (Penpie, a protocol built on Pendle, lost ~$27M).

morpho-blue.label: Morpho Blue (isolated market)
morpho-blue.basis: Immutable core, formally verified; exploits of >=$100M lending protocols in the record took <1% of TVL (Aave V3 $0.9M, Venus $3.7M). Mean ~9% of collateral, deliberately above that record.

oracle.basis: Counts misconfigured / stale / predictable oracle exploits only (spot-price manipulation of thin tokens does not apply to a PT oracle), over Lending + CDP protocols >= $1M. Severity: the reading drops ~10% on average, enough to liquidate a high-LTV loop with no real loss of value.

frequency.basis: Exploit frequency = hacks over the last 5 years of protocols in the same current-TVL tier (<$10M, $10M-$100M, >=$100M), all categories pooled, / (protocols in that tier x 5); x the category's rate relative to all categories (clipped 0.5-2); x an age factor. Survivorship: hacked protocols that died are missing from the denominator's tier, which biases small tiers up, not the >=$100M tier.

pt_stress_basis: During an underlying depeg, PT trades below its redemption value as LPs withdraw from the Pendle pool: market-tracking oracles see the depeg amplified by 1.5x.
tail_budget_basis: Recommend reducing when CVaR99, the average loss of the worst 1 % of simulated months, exceeds 50 % of equity.

incident.basis: D90. Incident mode sizes a partial sale so that liquidation sits this far beyond the oracle drop the incident causes: one point of margin, so a small further move does not liquidate the reduced position. exit_min_gain (D101): for a vault depositor, leaving first is recommended only when it cuts the incident's loss by at least 5 %; a depositor that is most of the vault loses about the same either way.
incident.breakeven_basis: D142-D144: exiting now forgoes the vault's net yield (Morpho API avgNetApy, rewards included) on what can leave, over --horizon days; it saves the difference between the loss if the depositor stays and if it leaves first. p* = carry forgone / loss saved, over the horizon; yearly = 1 - (1 - p*)^(365 / horizon).

watch.basis: D26. Shares are of the vault's total assets; the oracle move is between two consecutive state reads; large_flow_info: a deposit or withdrawal by someone else above 1% of total assets. full_state_every_blocks (D61): a live batch with no event re-reads only oracle prices, totalAssets, realAssets, idle cash and the depositor's gates; the full read runs on any event and at least every 25 blocks (~5 min), which bounds the staleness of the borrow rate and of anything changed without an event the poller fetches.
watch.concentration_basis: D129. BorrowerConcentration warns when one borrower holds at least half a market's debt, or the market has fewer than 5 borrowers, for markets holding at least utilization_min_share of a vault. In most RockawayX RWA markets one or two loopers hold the debt (ROCK-VAULT-DEP.md §6): the vault then depends on them repaying more than on liquidations.
watch.divergence_basis: D97. The oracle-versus-market check (OracleDivergence) runs with every batch's oracle prices and DefiLlama prices at most 25 blocks old (~5 min), instead of only at the 300-block refresh: a synthetic dollar fell 97 % in 17 minutes (USR, Mar 2026).
watch.drain_basis: D70, D72. drain_buy_cost: the cost c of buying the collateral at the drain's size, in d* = 1 - LLTV / (1 + c); 0.5 % is low on purpose (a lower cost gives an earlier, more conservative threshold) and is not measured per token. drain_margin: warn when the collateral's discount to the oracle is within 2 points of d*. drain_check_every_blocks: DefiLlama's prices are re-read every 25 blocks (~5 min); oracle prices come with every state read.
watch.exit_queue_basis: D64, D66. exit_queue_phi: the share of the other depositors' assets assumed to leave before you in a run, Team 2's single parameter phi; 0.5 is a middle case with no data behind it. exit_queue_stuck_warn: warn when at least half of the position would be stuck if every contract holder (vault, fund, multisig) withdrew first; critical when, in addition, the vault already carries unrealised bad debt.
watch.feed_band_basis: D183 (plan/2026-10-11-fork-demo.plan.md). A custom feed whose minAnswer/maxAnswer are readable on the feed is reported (FeedBand) when its floor lies within this fraction below its latest answer. mGLOeuro/EUR (Midas, read 2026-10-11) has a band of 90,000-110,000 EUR around 100,000 and no setter, so a fund loss above 10 % reaches the Belem market's oracle only after an upgrade behind a 48 h timelock. Chainlink OCR bands are not exposed on the proxy and never trigger.

graph.sibling_basis: D79. A market with less than $1M supplied (its TVL, Morpho API supplyAssetsUsd) is never a sibling, and at most 10 per held market are kept, the largest borrow first, since borrow is what liquidations sell. Raised from a $100k borrow floor on 2026-10-10 at the person's request, to keep graph runs short: the example graph (Sentora RLUSD Main and two borrowers) went from 65 siblings and 8 to 12 minutes against the free RPC. Held markets are never filtered by size.

oracle_getters.basis: Pendle PendleChainlinkOracle: a TWAP of the Pendle AMM (900 s on PT-reUSD), so a pool move reaches the price
Pendle linear-discount oracle: a deterministic discount to maturity, no market input

oracle_patterns.basis: Pendle linear discount to maturity (contract name)
net asset value reported by the issuer (contract name)

Midas custom aggregator feed: the issuer's admin publishes the NAV by transaction (contract name, e.g. MGloEuroCustomAggregatorFeed behind an upgradeable proxy; mGLOeuro read 100,000 EUR on 2026-08-04 and 2026-09-23, its only two rounds)
PT discount lowered only by the SY's own accounting losses (exchangeRate against pyIndexStored), no market input (verified source, 2026-10-10)
RedStone fundamental feed: the issuer's redemption value, not a market price
an exchange rate between a token and its underlying, not a market price
net asset value reported by the issuer
a discount schedule or a discounted NAV, not a market price

graph.oracle_basis: D82-D84. One oracle input, first rule that applies: a base vault is an exchange rate; a composite (FEED_1/FEED_2) or wrapper (innerOracle) takes its children's class, price-tracking if one is; a structural getter of oracle_getters; at least oracle_history_min past rounds readable over the last oracle_history_rounds: price-tracking when falls are at least oracle_fall_share of the changes (probe 2026-10-10: USDC/USD, USDS/USD and ETH/USD fell 9-14 times in 24 rounds, three exchange-rate and NAV feeds never fell); no history and an answer of exactly 1.0: pegged; a case-insensitive pattern of oracle_patterns in description() or the verified contract name (Etherscan, optional); otherwise not classified.

exit_liquidity.basis: KyberSwap aggregator quotes of a sale into USDC on Ethereum, measured 2026-10-11 (docs/analysis/ROCK-VAULT-DEP.md §7). route: none = no route at 0.1M USD, thin = price impact above thin_impact at 1M USD, deep = otherwise. impact: the price impact at each sale size in USD (null: no route). A liquidator who cannot sell the collateral does not liquidate (D131). Re-measure before relying on it; add any token by address.

pharos.basis: Pharos (pharos.watch, TokenBrice, MIT) public dependency graph, keyless, methodology v10.16 / model v9 as read on 2026-10-11. Grades are Pharos's judgement, not probabilities: shown, never used as a number in a loss. Backing weights are Pharos's reserve shares (live-reserve or curated-reserve provenance). docs/risk-assessment/outside-providers.md
pharos.ids_basis: each address's symbol() read on-chain on 2026-10-11 and matched to the Pharos id by name and issuer; iUSD and reUSD are ambiguous by symbol (three iUSD, two reUSD ids)
pharos.groups_basis: chain, DEX and wide bridge groups (Ethereum: 202 coins, LayerZero: 33) say nothing about one issuer; a group of at most 12 coins sharing a mint key, an upgrade admin, a reserve issuer or a redemption rail does

edge_rules.basis: a loan token's price move changes no amount owed or supplied in that token, and the vault counts in it
the same for a move inherited from an underlying
D115: a feed reads the market it tracks (a Pendle TWAP its PT's pool, a 'SYM / USD' feed that pair): a move of that market moves the reading
Morpho ChainlinkOracleV2: price = base vault x base feeds / (quote vault x quote feeds); a base feed reading m x moves the price by m
a quote feed divides the price: reading m x moves it by 1/m
a base feed following its market moves the oracle with it
D116: a quote feed following the loan token rescales the oracle and the collateral's worth alike in that token: no effect in loan units
a frozen base feed stops the oracle following its collateral
the oracle applies the vault's accounting rate (convertToAssets), not the share's market price
the vault's accounting rate does not follow its asset's market either
a market liquidates on its oracle's reading
a market liquidates on its oracle's reading
a frozen oracle no longer follows its collateral
D115: the oracle reads its collateral's market through a tracked feed (rule tracks), not here; the collateral's worth still moves
a price-tracking oracle with no tracked input is assumed to follow its collateral's market: a fall liquidates borrowers
a constant-price oracle ignores the market: a fall liquidates nobody and leaves insolvent debt
D108: an oracle not classified is treated as not following, the lender's worse case (no liquidation, a silent loss)
D115: a move inherited from an underlying changes the collateral's worth; no oracle reading its own market or its accounting rate sees it
D113: liquidations can sell only what the collateral's market absorbs
an ERC-4626 share redeems into its asset: a move of the asset's market changes the share's worth, not its own market or its rate
a move inherited by the asset passes on to its share

D115: a PT is worth its underlying at maturity, so a move of the underlying's market changes the PT's worth; the pool prices PT against the underlying (PT_TO_ASSET / PT_TO_SY), so the pool price, which a Pendle oracle reads, does not move
a move inherited by the underlying passes on to the PT
PT liquidators sell the underlying they receive: if its market cannot absorb it, the PT's liquidations cannot complete
a move of the Pendle pool's own price is the PT's market price
a move inherited through the pool passes on to the PT
the underlying's exit limit passes on to the PT
liquidators offer the seized collateral for sale into its market
a PT sold into its pool comes out as underlying
liquidators sell that underlying for dollars
a market's loss is shared by its suppliers pro rata to their supply
a vault's loss is shared by its depositors pro rata to their shares (D110; the run order comes with step 2)

node_rules.basis: D107: Blue liquidations, write-offs, insolvent debt and the drain; D113, D114: only what the collateral's market absorbs is sold, and offers ratchet
a frozen oracle or feed keeps its reading

D112, D113: an asset's own market price takes the impact of what is offered into it, from real Pendle quotes (a PT's pool; an underlying's sale for dollars), up to its capacity; a PT stops falling where a buyer holding to maturity earns stress_yield (50 % APY, judgement)
inputs combined: factors multiply, sales and losses add, exits take the smallest

engine.basis: D104-D116 (plan 2026-10-10-propagation-engine). Rules are tried in order; the first edge rule whose effect, direction, rel and criteria match carries the effect, and no match stops it. --rules <file> puts a file's edge_rules and node_rules first. eps: relative change below which an input is not propagated again; max_evaluations bounds the loop. quote_sizes_x_liquidity: the sale sizes of the Pendle quote ladders the graph records per PT, as multiples of the pool's liquidity, at most quote_max_usd (Pendle refuses above 100M USD); a size Pendle cannot route (MarketProportionTooHigh) ends the ladder and sets the capacity at the last size that went through; capacity_min_ratio: a ladder's capacity is where the marginal price falls under this share of spot or the amount received stops growing (2026-10-10: PT-reUSD into reUSD loses 0.57 % at $25M, reUSD into USDC stops near $12M). depth_usd: a depth for the constant_product comparison model only.

nexus.basis: Nexus Mutual public API (api.nexusmutual.io/v2, keyless), read 2026-10-11. A product is mapped to the tokens whose issuer protocol it covers; the wording (IPFS annex of each product) decides what pays: Single Protocol Cover pays on a smart-contract exploit of that protocol, not on an issuer's NAV markdown or a borrower's default. Shown next to the breakeven probability, never used in a verdict.
nexus.loading_basis: a cover price is the expected payout times a loading for capital cost and margin; 2-5 brackets it (docs/analysis/EXTERNAL_SOURCE.md §7.5: a loading of 3 brings the Nexus-implied depeg frequencies of USDe and USDS back to the internal ones)

feeds.basis: D156: a feed is stale when its last update is older than stale_factor × its own median update interval (read from its past rounds) and stale_min_hours (a daily heartbeat plus an hour's margin); without round history, older than no_history_max_days. Chainlink's heartbeat and deviation threshold are off-chain configuration, so the observed rhythm stands in for them. ROCK-VAULT-DEP.md: mGLOeuro's NAV feed was 17.5 days old on 2026-10-11.

tvl.basis: D158-D160: DefiLlama /protocols (already the source of the incident base rates), the snapshot's copy offline (fixtures/snapshot, as of its date). A protocol's TVL against all of DeFi and against its DefiLlama category; the brief's 'protocols concentrating a large share of on-chain TVL'. Shares are of the total over every chain, as /protocols gives no per-chain split in the cached copy.
tvl.warn_basis: 2 % of all DeFi is a top-10 protocol (Lido 4.1 %, Aave V3 2.9 %, Morpho Blue 1.9 % on 2026-10-10); a quarter of a category is a dominant venue for that kind of risk; a category share counts only for a category of at least warn_category_min_usd (fx Protocol is 57 % of a 220M category)
